item.research_question: How does the high-pressure phase transformation behavior of a suction-cast ordered eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) compare to that of additively manufactured (L-PBF) EHEA, and what role does the initial B2 phase play in the transformation mechanism?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA), specifically suction-cast samples containing ordered B2 and disordered FCC phases
item.processing_route: Arc melting of raw elements (99.9 wt% purity) followed by re-melting six times (30 s at 600 A) and rapid suction casting into a water-cooled copper mold (3 mm × 10 mm × 50 mm) with an estimated cooling rate of ~10^2 K/s
item.test_conditions: Static high pressure in a diamond anvil cell (250 micron culet) using synchrotron X-ray diffraction (wavelength 0.42459 Å) up to 73 GPa at ambient temperature; molecular dynamics simulations with isotropic pressure applied at 0.65 GPa/ps up to 130 GPa
key_findings: The B2 to FCC phase transformation in suction-cast EHEA is completed by 3 GPa, which is roughly ten times lower than the 21 GPa required for L-PBF synthesized samples.
At 73 GPa, the material is fully in the FCC phase with a lattice parameter reduced to 3.311 Å.
The FCC phase is retained on decompression from 73 GPa to ambient pressure, indicating an irreversible transformation.
The bulk modulus of the FCC phase was determined to be 184.4 ± 2.8 GPa with a pressure derivative of 3.85 ± 0.27.
Pressure-recovered samples show only FCC grains with no specific orientation relationship maintained with respect to the starting sample.
The B2 phase is enriched in Nickel (~40 at%) and Aluminum (~25 at%), while the surrounding FCC phase is enriched in Cr, Fe, and Co (~20 at% each).
Molecular dynamics simulations show the B2 to FCC transition completes at 130 GPa in the model, involving shear along specific directions to accommodate volume shrinkage.
item.mechanism: The presence of the ordered B2 phase aids in the formation of the FCC phase under high pressure; the transition follows the classic Kurdjumov-Sachs (K-S) orientation relationship ({111}FCC || {110}BCC and <110>FCC || <111>BCC) and involves shear to accommodate volume shrinkage, with the interphase boundary remaining essentially stationary.
item.limitations: The study notes the absence of an accurate interatomic potential for the complex EHEA AlCoCrFeNi2.1, necessitating the use of a simplified ternary FeCuNi model for molecular dynamics simulations.
item.future_work: The authors state that high pressure serves as an important enabling technology to induce irreversible phase transformations and microstructures to improve physical and mechanical properties, implying further study on property enhancement.
quotes: The B2 to FCC phase transformation is completed by 3 GPa in sharp contrast to BCC to FCC phase transition of 21 GPa in additively manufactured EHEA samples.
The B2 phase was observed to be enriched in Nickel and Aluminum while the surrounding FCC phase is enriched in Fe, Cr and Co.
